messages.author: 7f3082874cbcb368
messages.subject: getting error in init section: Error: unexpected '[[' in "[["
parts:
Hi group,

I could not solve the problem posted before. I am getting the same error (i.e., Error: unexpected '[[' in "[["). I tried using R and R studio. MplusAutomation package was installed and loaded before running this code. If you want to try this on your PC, you can use the dataset below:

library(foreign)
dat = read.csv("http://www.math.smith.edu/r/data/help.csv")
mydata=dat[,c(71,74,79,84)]
#then you can save it to your PC

I adapted this code from http://sas-and-r.blogspot.com/2011/02/example-824-mplusautomation-and-mplus.html

It is very important for me to run this code because it is very similar to my simulation design. Can anyone help me with this? Why am I getting this error?

Thanks in advance!

Sedat

On Thu, Feb 14, 2013 at 10:31 AM, Sedat Sen <sedat...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Josh,

Sorry for not sending the full code before. Here is my full code:


[[init]]
iterators = classes;
classes = 1:4;
dir = "C:/Users/Sedatsen/Desktop/MplusAutomation";
filename = "mplus-[[classes]]-class-.inp";
outputDirectory = [[dir]];
[[/init]]
TITLE: [[classes]]-class
DATA: FILE IS mplus2.dat;
VARIABLE: NAMES ARE homeless cesdcut satreat linkstatus;
CLASSES = c ([[classes]]);
CATEGORICAL = all;
ANALYSIS: TYPE = MIXTURE; 
STARTS = 2000 200;
STITERATIONS=1000;
OUTPUT: TECH1 TECH10;
SAVEDATA: FILE IS "mplus-[[classes]]-class.cprob";
SAVE IS CPROB;




On Thu, Feb 14, 2013 at 10:30 AM, Joshua Wiley <jwiley...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Sedat,

Can you send us the full r code you are trying and the Mplus input?

If you types [[init]] at the R console, that is not a valid command.

Cheers,

Josh

On Feb 14, 2013, at 6:45, sedat...@gmail.com wrote:

Dear MplusAutomation users,

I am very new to this package. I was just trying to learn it by replicating some ready to use codes. Somehow I could not do anything with init section due to an error.


Does anyone have any idea why I am getting the error below?

> [[init]]
Error: unexpected '[[' in "[["



>[[/init]]
Error: unexpected '[[' in "                                                [["


Everything between these two inits looked OK. Am I missing any packages?



Thanks in advance,

Sedat

Hi Sedat,

Did you put your code in a *separate* template file? None of it will
work entered straight into R. It has to be in a file that you process
with the createModels() function.

Cheers,

Josh

messages.subject: Re: getting error in init section: Error: unexpected '[[' in "[["
parts:
I am getting a similar problem using Mplus Automation, both in R and RStudio. The file I'm trying to run is for a demonstration for my work group, so it's simple:

[[init]]
iterators = xvars ;
xvars = 1:3 ;
xvarnames#xvars = "x1" "x2" "x3" ;
filename = "[[demo#xvars]].inp" ;
outputDirectory="M:/mplusauto2" ;
[[init/]]
TITLE: Predict Y2 from Y1 and [[xvarnames#xvars]]
DATA: File is ex3.11.dat;
VARIABLE: NAMES ARE y1-y3 x1-x3;
Missing are all (-9999);
USEVARIABLES ARE y1 y2 [[xvarnames#xvars]];
MODEL: y2 ON y1 [[xvarnames$xvars]];

I created this .txt file in Notepad, and am running it in an R script in Rstudio.
The error message is

> createModels("template2.txt")
Error in createModels("template2.txt") : 
  Unable to find init section in template file.

I looked at the source code, and used -grep- in Linux to try to find the "[[init]]" string, and it is there...grep finds it.
I also checked the rest of my code and it seems fine.

Can you help? Thanks.

Cathy

messages.subject: Re: getting error in init section: Error: unexpected '[[' in "[["
parts:
Hi Cathy,

Make sure your init section terminates [[/init]] not [[init/]].

Also, this tag looks incorrect: [[demo#xvars]] because demo is not defined as a variable anywhere. I suspect you mean: "demo[[xvars]].inp"

Michael

On Sunday, June 15, 2014 1:10:00 PM UTC-4, michael.hallquist wrote:
Hi Cathy,

Make sure your init section terminates [[/init]] not [[init/]].

Also, this tag looks incorrect: [[demo#xvars]] because demo is not defined as a variable anywhere. I suspect you mean: "demo[[xvars]].inp"

Michael

On Friday, June 13, 2014 5:08:44 PM UTC-4, Cathy Antonakos wrote:
I am getting a similar problem using Mplus Automation, both in R and RStudio. The file I'm trying to run is for a demonstration for my work group, so it's simple:

[[init]]
iterators = xvars ;

xvarnames#xvars = "x1" "x2" "x3" ;
filename = "[[demo#xvars]].inp" ;
outputDirectory="M:/mplusauto2" ;
[[init/]]
TITLE: Predict Y2 from Y1 and [[xvarnames#xvars]]
DATA: File is ex3.11.dat;
VARIABLE: NAMES ARE y1-y3 x1-x3;
Missing are all (-9999);
USEVARIABLES ARE y1 y2 [[xvarnames#xvars]];
MODEL: y2 ON y1 [[xvarnames$xvars]];

I created this .txt file in Notepad, and am running it in an R script in Rstudio.
The error message is

> createModels("template2.txt")

  Unable to find init section in template file.

I looked at the source code, and used -grep- in Linux to try to find the "[[init]]" string, and it is there...grep finds it.
I also checked the rest of my code and it seems fine.

Can you help? Thanks.

Cathy
